general.demo_title: Recording Quality Score of a Walk with U-Turn Measured with Four Inertial Sensors
input_description: A trial of the test standing – 10 m walk – U-turn – 10 m walk back – standing, recorded with inertial sensors on the head (optional), the lower back, the left foot and the right foot.

Raw files (one per sensor): text tables with the columns PacketCounter, Acc_X, Acc_Y, Acc_Z, Gyr_X, Gyr_Y, Gyr_Z, not filtered and not corrected. The head file may be left empty: the head indicators are then not computed.

Segmentation file (JSON): the results of the two IPOL segmentation demos gathered in one object, {"uturn": {content of uturn.json}, "gait_events": {content of gait_events.json}}, given by the U-turn segmentation demo (lower-back file) and the MP-DTW gait events demo (foot files). The result file of one demo alone is accepted: the other part is then scored 0, with the reason.

Recommended order: run this demo first without the segmentation file, to get the corrected files (axes in the classic frame and, for the lower back, X axis aligned on the vertical); run the U-turn and gait-event demos on these corrected files; then run this demo again on the raw files with the segmentation file: the score keeps the trace of the placement and judges the segmentation actually used.
param_description: Acquisition frequency of the sensors and units of the raw files (automatic: recognised from the order of magnitude of the signals).

run: python3 $bin/main.py -i0 input_0.txt -i1 input_1.txt -i2 input_2.txt -i3 input_3.txt -i4 input_4.json -freq $freq -acc_unit $acc_unit -gyr_unit $gyr_unit

contents: No head sensor was given: the head indicators are not computed and do not enter the scores.

results.label:
Construction of the score

The signals behind each group of indicators, with the quality of each indicator.

Corrected files

Same columns and samples as the raw files, axes in the classic frame and, for the lower back, X axis aligned on the vertical: input of the U-turn and gait-event demos and of the gait parameters.
